newsitem.title: CHINA: China Hong Kong group discusses panel nominees.
newsitem.headline: China Hong Kong group discusses panel nominees.

text.p: The Chinese committee overseeing Hong Kong's 1997 return to mainland rule met in Beijing on Friday to discuss nominees to a panel to select the territory's first top official under Chinese rule.
Members of the Preparatory Committee were meeting to propose the names of favoured candidates for the much-coveted seats on the Selection Committee, but would make no decisions, officials said.

"This time the committee members will put forward the candidates they have their eyes on," said Kang Guowei, an official with the Hong Kong and Macau Affairs Office under China's State Council, or cabinet.
The Preparatory Committee would meet again in November to choose the final 400 members of the Selection Committee, Kang said.

In September, nearly 6,000 Hong Kong residents applied for a place on the panel, which will pick the first person to lead the British colony after the territory reverts to Chinese rule at midnight on June 30, 1997.
Kang declined to give details about nominees or what criteria the Preparatory Committee would use in the final selection process.
The session ends on Saturday, he said.
